subject: Service confidence update: hosted API elevated error-rate (us-east)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@stellarnet.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Service confidence update: hosted API elevated error-rate (us-east)

Hi Maya --

Quick heads-up: starting around 08:45 PDT we began seeing an elevated error-rate (502/504s) and p95 generation latency spikes for a subset of tokens hitting the hosted-generation endpoint in the us-east region. Early scope: ~7% of requests for StellarNet saw intermittent failures or elongated tails; other customers unaffected.

What we know so far:
- Impact window: ~08:45 - ongoing
- Symptoms: increased 502/504s, p95 up to ~2.4s (normal ~0.8s) for streamed generations
- Surface area: hosted inference (generation) / us-east pool only

Immediate mitigation in progress: our on-call runbook triggered a rollback of a routing change that was being staged for capacity optimization; we also throttled a small prefetch fanout that correlated with the spikes. Early telemetry shows request success rate improving but we want to validate stability.

Next steps (short):
1) We are keeping the rollback in place until telemetry is stable for one hour.
2) We will proactively route new requests away from the affected pool if we see any recurrence.
3) Postmortem draft and timeline will be shared by EOD.

We appreciate the quick flag from your side this morning — thanks for the signal. I will send a clear follow-up once we confirm full recovery.

Attachments: redwood_incident_summary_draft.pdf (initial timeline snapshot)

Regards,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service confidence update: hosted API elevated error-rate (us-east)

Ben — thanks for the update and the draft. A couple of quick technical clarifications for customer-facing language:

- Root cause appears to be a staged router policy change that widened prefetch fanout to an experimental edge pool; when combined with a small config mismatch on KV cache eviction it amplified tail work, leading to transient amplification of in-flight requests and upstream 502s.
- We rolled back the router policy at 09:12 PDT; the prefetch throttle was applied at 09:18 PDT. The earliest customer-visible improvements began around 09:28 PDT.

Suggest we keep the message to the customer focused and non-technical for now: state that we rolled back a routing change, applied a temporary throttle, and are validating. If Stable for an hour, offer a follow-up postmortem w/ timeline and any credit actions.

I'll attach a CSV timeline snippet and a short ops note.

Laura
Director, Platform Reliability
redwood.com

Maya —

Follow-up: We rolled back the router policy and applied a temporary prefetch throttle this morning; as of 12:55 PDT your observed success-rate has returned to baseline and p95 looks within normal bounds. We will keep the throttle in place for monitoring and then stage a controlled re-introduction of the optimization after further validation.

What changed (short):
- Rollback of routing policy (09:12 PDT) + prefetch throttle (09:18 PDT)
- Measured customer impact window: 08:45 — 09:28 PDT
- Current status: healthy (no ongoing errors in StellarNet's request slice)

Next steps:
- We will publish a concise postmortem draft to you by EOD (attached) and publish a public incident note on our status page: https://status.redwood.in/incident/2028-06-us-east-elevated-errors
- If you would like a dedicated post-incident review with our reliability team, I'm happy to coordinate — please let me know times that work.

Attachments: redwood_incident_summary_draft.pdf, timeline_snippet.csv

Apologies for the disruption this morning and thank you for the rapid signal — it helped us shorten the window.

Best,
Ben Carter
